recordings.previousText: A setback isn't final while the position can still be held. The earlier setback no longer decides things, because this move makes the position playable. Connecting those two moments is the useful part of the lesson.
recordings.text: A setback isn't final while the game can still be held. After the earlier one, the position is playable again, and the moves in between are worth going through slowly.
recordings.reason: A move never raises its own evaluation; the opponent's moves made the game playable again, so the take no longer credits this move or the learner.

recordings.previousText: A king behind its own pieces can find every escape square blocked by its own side. That's the back-rank mate idea in this move: the king is boxed in with no room to step out. Its own cover is what limits it.
recordings.text: A king behind its own pieces can end up with no way off its back rank. That's the back-rank mate idea in this move: the king is boxed in, with no room to step out.
recordings.reason: A back-rank mate checks along the king's rank, so the square beside the king toward the checker is never blocked by an own piece; the take now says the king is boxed in behind its own pieces.
